TargetRLF1: When gonorrhea infections aren’t treated, the bacteria can spread, causing more symptoms. Specific symptoms depend on the area of the body affected by the bacteria. Gonorrhea may affect women and men differently. In women, it may show little to no symptoms for long periods of time. For men, two to five days after infection, they may experience pain or burning on urination, white or yellow discharge from penis and swollen testes. In women, symptoms can be subtle and may include pain or burning on urination, vaginal discharge and vaginal bleeding between periods and during intercourse. If the infection is in the throat it may cause redness, pain and a sore feeling, similar to a sore throat. Anal infections can cause discharge, bleeding, itchiness, soreness and painful bowel movements. In babies, eye infection can cause redness, pain, soreness, wounds in the eye, tearing, swollen eyelids and pus discharge, which can lead to blindness if untreated. If the gonorrhea infection is spread throughout the body, it can lead to joint pain, skin lesions, fever, and heart and brain complications. Gonorrhea may affect women and men differently. Education and awareness campaigns aimed at reducing HIV stigma are also essential to improving the overall well-being of youth living with HIV.

TargetRLF1: Human immunodeficiency virus is a zoonosis – an infection that originated in animals and passed into human hosts. It is closely related to the simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) found in chimpanzees in central Africa. SIV probably entered the human population as a result of hunting chimpanzees. It is plausible that transmission could have occurred through a hunter being wounded and blood from a chimpanzee entering his bloodstream. Chimpanzees avoid humans wherever possible, so it is likely that SIVcpz crossed into humans as a result of human encroachment into forest areas. TargetRLF1: A chlamydia test detects the bacteria that cause chlamydia, a sexually transmitted infection (STI) so as to get treatment. Your provider takes a sample of urine or secretions from your vagina, penis or rectum and sends it to a lab for testing. Results are usually ready in a day. Less often, providers use a cell culture to test for chlamydia. In this case, your provider swabs/wipes your vagina, urethra or anus to collect a sample and send it to a lab for testing. If bacteria are present, it indicates an infection. Providers may choose this type of chlamydia test to detect infections in the anus. Or they may use a cell culture to see how chlamydia treatments are working. Because of the possibility of multiple sexually transmitted infections, all patients with any sexually transmitted disease (STD) should be evaluated for chlamydial infection. There are no risks involved with these tests. Rarely the results of the tests may be inconclusive or unclear and you may need to give another sample. You should test for chlamydia for early detection and institution of treatment. If not treated appropriately and timely, chlamydia can result into severe complications like PID, fertility problems, and pregnancy negative effects. It is therefore important that you test early to identify the infection if it is there, treat it and prevent spreading to your partner. TargetRLF1: A swab test. Your doctor or nurse uses a cotton swab to take a fluid sample from an infected place (cervix, rectum, or throat). The fluid is then tested for gonorrhea. Women are not usually asked to provide a urine sample to check for gonorrhoea because this is a less-accurate test for women. 1.        Culture performed on an intraurethral swab specimen is preferred in settings where collecting such specimens is acceptable and transport and storage conditions are suitable for culture. Collection of exudate for N. gonorrhoeae culture at the urethral meatus without insertion of the swab into the urethra is sufficient when exudate is present. Culture performed on an intraurethral swab specimen is preferred because it facilitates additional testing, which is critical for monitoring for antimicrobial resistance. When culture sensitivity might be compromised because of problems in maintaining appropriate transport and storage conditions, a NAAT or nucleic acid hybridization test can be performed on an intraurethral swab specimen.2.        A NAAT or nucleic acid hybridization test performed on an intraurethral swab specimen or a NAAT performed on urine are acceptable tests for screening. Intraurethral swab specimens are often unacceptable to males who do not have symptoms of urethritis (89--91). In such cases, NAATs performed on urine to detect N. gonorrhoeae have adequate sensitivity for use in screening. Only a limited number of published studies have addressed whether NAATs perform better with urethral swab specimens than with urine in males with asymptomatic infection. One study of asymptomatic males reported that a NAAT was substantially less sensitive with urine than with urethral swabs; furthermore, NAATs were less sensitive with either specimen among males with asymptomatic infection than with symptomatic infection (54,56).

TargetRLF1: Puberty in Males: Puberty is the period of development when a boy's body changes into an adult male body capable of reproduction. It is typically marked by physical changes and hormonal shifts. Effects on Male Reproductive System: Testes: The testes begin to grow and produce sperm, a process known as spermatogenesis. Penis: The penis grows and matures. Prostate Gland: The prostate gland enlarges and starts producing fluids that nourish and protect sperm. Secondary Sexual Characteristics: Males develop secondary sexual characteristics such as facial hair, deepening voice, increased muscle mass, and growth of the Adam's apple. These changes are driven by hormonal changes, particularly testosterone, which is responsible for the development of male reproductive organs and secondary sexual characteristics. During puberty, girls' breasts and boys' chests might start to grow. This is due to the hormones estrogen and testosterone. Estrogen causes breast development in girls, leading to fuller breasts. Boys might notice some swelling or tenderness around their nipples, which is also normal. It's all part of the changes that happen during puberty. Hormones are responsible for the many changes you're experiencing during puberty. They're the reason why you're growing taller, developing secondary sexual characteristics, experiencing mood swings, and more. Hormones are like the body's internal "switches" that turn on different aspects of growth and development.

HSV-2 can be transmitted even if the skin looks normal and is often transmitted in the absence of symptoms. In rare circumstances, herpes (HSV-1 and HSV-2) can be transmitted from mother to child during vaginal delivery, causing neonatal herpes. It can also cause genital herpes. Most adults are infected with HSV-1. Type 2 (HSV-2) spreads by sexual contact and causes genital herpes. Most people have no symptoms or only mild symptoms. The infection can cause painful blisters or ulcers that can recur over time. Medicines can reduce symptoms but can’t cure the infection.Recurrent symptoms of both oral and genital herpes may be distressing. Genital herpes may also be stigmatizing and have an impact on sexual relationships. However, in time, most people with either kind of herpes adjust to living with the infection. TargetRLF1: A chlamydia also known as Chlamydial Genitourinary infection test detects the bacteria that cause chlamydia, a sexually transmitted infection (STI). This test tells you if you have the chlamydia infection so that you can get treat treatment and avoid complications.. Your provider takes a sample of urine or secretions from your vagina, penis or rectum and sends it to a lab for testing using a test called NAATs (short for nucleic acid amplification tests), which is very accurate and easy to take. Results are usually ready in a day. Less often, providers use a cell culture to test for chlamydia. In this case, your provider swabs your vagina, urethra or anus to collect a sample of fluid and cells. They send the cells to a lab to test. If bacteria are present, they will grow, which indicates an infection. Providers may choose this type of chlamydia test to detect infections in the anus. Or they may use a cell culture to see how chlamydia treatments are working. Your need for testing depends on your personal risk for getting Chlamydia. There are no risks involved with these tests. Rarely the results of the tests may be inconclusive or unclear and you may need to give another sample. You should get tested regularly if you have unprotected sex with a new partner, multiple partners or a partner who has an STI. You should also get tested if you have symptoms or you are pregnant. Many people with Chlamydia don't have symptoms. Because of the possibility of multiple sexually transmitted infections, all patients with any sexually transmitted disease (STD) should be evaluated for chlamydial infection. Individuals with symptoms of Genital Herpes or Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV), also known as herpes should abstain from sexual activity while experiencing symptoms. Both HSV-1 and HSV-2 are most contagious when sores are present but can also be transmitted when no symptoms are felt or visible. For sexually active people, consistent and correct use of condoms is the best way to prevent genital herpes and other STIs. Condoms reduce the risk; however, HSV infection can still occur through contact with genital or anal areas not covered by the condom. Medical male circumcision can provide life-long partial protection against HSV-2 infection, as well as against HIV and human papillomavirus (HPV). Pregnant women with symptoms of genital herpes should inform their health care providers. Preventing acquisition of HSV-2 infection is particularly important for women in late pregnancy when the risk for neonatal herpes is greatest. The only way to completely avoid STIs is to not have vaginal, anal, or oral sex. If you are sexually active, you can do the following things to lower your chances of getting Genital Herpes or Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV), also known as herpes:•        Being in a long-term mutually monogamous relationship with a partner who does not have herpes.•        Using condoms the right way every time you have sex.Be aware that not all herpes sores occur in areas that a condom can cover. Also, the skin can release the virus (shed) from areas that do not have a visible herpes sore. For these reasons, condoms may not fully protect you from getting herpes. If your sex partner(s) has/have genital herpes, you can lower your risk of getting it if:•        Your partner takes an anti-herpes medicine every day. TargetRLF1: While some people with Genital Herpes or Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV), also known as herpes will never have any symptoms, other people can develop symptoms within a few weeks of being infected. Common oral herpes symptoms include blisters (cold sores) or open sores (ulcers) in or around the mouth or lips. Most people notice a group or cluster of blisters or ulcers (lesions). These lesions burn and can be painful. They can appear on the buttocks, anus or thighs, on the vulva or vagina in women, and on the penis or scrotum in men. Often, before the lesions appear, patients describe a prodrome, characterized by a tingling or burning sensation in the area where the lesions will develop that can be noticed during urination, along with itching or discomfort in the genital area. You can also have the following symptoms, Blisters on the mouth or lips, Fever, headache or pain in the joints, Trouble urinating. In case of Neonatal Herpes, signs that your baby may have herpes are:irritability, blisters anywhere on her body, trouble breathing, grunting, blue appearance (cyanosis), rapid breathing, short periods of no breathing, jaundice, bleeding easily. People can have repeated outbreaks over time (‘recurrences’). These are usually shorter and less severe than the first outbreak. Herpes is a lifelong sexually transmitted infection, that cannot be cured. However, the number of outbreaks/recurrences may reduce over time. TargetRLF1: Male Reproductive Organs: Testes: These are the male gonads responsible for producing sperm and testosterone. Epididymis: This is a coiled tube where sperm mature and are stored. Vas Deferens: A tube that carries mature sperm from the epididymis to the urethra. Prostate Gland: Produces fluids that nourish and protect sperm. Penis: The male organ of copulation and the exit point for urine and semen. Female Reproductive Organs: Ovaries: The female gonads that produce eggs (ova) and female sex hormones (estrogen and progesterone). Fallopian Tubes: Tubes that transport eggs from the ovaries to the uterus. Fertilization of the egg by sperm usually occurs in the fallopian tubes. Uterus (Womb): The organ where a fertilized egg implants and develops into a fetus during pregnancy. Cervix: The lower part of the uterus that connects to the vagina. Vagina: The canal that leads from the uterus to the outside of the body. It serves as the birth canal during childbirth and also allows menstrual flow to exit the body. Menstruation, often called a period, is a natural process that happens in the female body. It's the shedding of the uterine lining, which occurs approximately once a month. This usually happens about once a month for three to seven days, varying from female to female. On average, the length of the menstrual cycle is 28 days, but generally this varies from woman to woman.  Regular cycles that are longer or shorter than this, from 21 to 35 days, are normal. Menstruation happens as a result of hormonal changes in the body, particularly estrogen and progesterone. These hormones cause the lining of the uterus to thicken each month in preparation for a potential pregnancy. If pregnancy does not occur, the lining is shed, and this is what you see as menstrual blood. During puberty, girls' breasts and boys' chests might start to grow. This is due to the hormones estrogen and testosterone. Estrogen causes breast development in girls, leading to fuller breasts. Boys might notice some swelling or tenderness around their nipples, which is also normal. It's all part of the changes that happen during puberty.

Oral sex; bacteria pass from one person’s mouth to their partner’s penis, vagina or anus, or vice versa. TargetRLF1: Key considerations include educating the society on the stigma that is around HIV patients. Knowing and understanding you and your status depends on the people around you. You should share your status with people who are not judgemental and who will not be isolated from you because of your status. Society at large needs to be educated on the stigmatization that is around HIV/AIDS patients. Antiretroviral therapy (ART) is the standard treatment for individuals living with HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus). While it is not mandatory to take ART, it is strongly recommended for most people diagnosed with HIV to manage their infection effectively and maintain good health. While ART is highly beneficial, it is a lifelong commitment. Once an individual starts ART, it is generally recommended to continue taking it as prescribed by a healthcare provider for the rest of their life. Stopping ART can result in a rebound of the virus, an increase in the viral load, and a decline in immune function. After approximately two decades of research on interventions to prevent HIV infection, there is a wealth of data documenting the results of HIV prevention efforts. The majority of existing prevention strategies are;  behavioral interventions, treatment of co-occurring conditions interventions, biomedical and technological interventions, and societal Interventions.

PEP ni salama na sio kila mtu ana madhara. Hata hivyo, baadhi ya watu wanaweza kupata kichefuchefu na kuhara.

Mtu hugundulika kuwa na UKIMWI anapokidhi vigezo maalum vikiwemo; Kuwa na hesabu ya seli za CD4 chini ya kiwango fulani (kwa kawaida chini ya seli 200/mm³ ya damu) au asilimia ya CD4 chini ya kiwango fulani. Kukuza baadhi ya magonjwa nyemelezi au magonjwa yanayofafanua UKIMWI, kama vile nimonia ya Pneumocystis (PCP), sarcoma ya Kaposi, au aina fulani za saratani. Watu wenye UKIMWI wana kinga dhaifu sana, hivyo kuwafanya wawe katika hatari kubwa ya kuambukizwa na magonjwa mbalimbali. UKIMWI ni hali mbaya ambayo inaweza kuhatarisha maisha ikiwa haitatibiwa. Ukimwi huambukizwa kwa kubadilishana majimaji fulani ya mwili. Majimaji ya mwili ni pamoja na damu, shahawa, maji maji ya ukeni, na maziwa ya mama.
